name: The Rep (Birmingham Repertory Theatre)
accessibility:
Fully step-free street level entrance directly off Centenary Square with automated power-assisted doors. Modern passenger lifts provide step-free access across all public auditorium levels, including the House (Main Stage), The Door, and The Studio. 
Dedicated wheelchair positions and level-transfer seats are available across every performance space. 
Modern accessible and Changing Places toilet facilities are located on the ground floor. Unisex cubicles located on the first floor allow plenty of space for parents with small children. 
Sennheiser radio frequency assistive hearing and induction loop systems are available to collect from the access desk.
relaxed:
The Rep is a national beacon for accessible theatre, scheduling dedicated Relaxed, Audio Described, Captioned, and British Sign Language (BSL) interpreted performances across all major productions and family seasons. 
Relaxed shows feature gently illuminated auditorium house lights, moderated sound effects without startling spikes or sudden pyrotechnics, and a flexible open-door policy allowing families to come and go freely. 
Quiet breakout zones and sensory chill-out rooms equipped with calming aids are provided in the foyers, supported by welcoming, specially trained front-of-house access hosts.
The Rep offers comfortable spacious seating throughout, with more than the average amount of leg room making it a fantastic venue for all.

name: Birmingham Hippodrome
accessibility: Level access to stalls and circle via lifts, accessible toilets on all levels including larger cubicles for grown ups and little ones,  booster seats available at entrance to stalls and circles and Sennheiser infrared hearing system installed.
relaxed: Regular relaxed and sensory-friendly performances scheduled for major pantomimes and touring family shows with chill-out zones in the foyer.

name: Wolverhampton Grand Theatre
accessibility:
Level access entrance from Lichfield Street into the foyer and Stalls. 
Modern passenger lift connects all three levels (Stalls, Dress Circle, Grand Circle). 8 dedicated wheelchair spaces across the auditorium and secure walking aid storage managed by front-of-house staff. 
 Toilets & Changing Facilities: 5 accessible adapted toilets distributed across all tiers with step-free access. Baby changing facilities are integrated within accessible cubicles. 
Sensory packs available on request (ear defenders and sensory toys). Designated calm/quiet breakout rooms with video monitors relaying the performance live for decompression. 
Pre-visit visual story packs and orientation sessions can be booked in advance.
relaxed:
Sensory-Friendly / Relaxed Shows: Regular relaxed and chilled stagings featuring low auditorium lighting, lowered sound volume, elimination of strobe/pyro effects, and complete freedom to exit and re-enter.
Sennheiser infrared assisted listening system, regular BSL-interpreted and captioned shows, plus Audio Described performances accompanied by tactile Touch Tours. 
Assistance dogs welcome in auditorium or cared for by volunteer staff.  
Access Scheme: Free Access Register offering essential companion tickets at no charge, priority booking, and discounted access pricing.

name: The Alexandra Theatre
accessibility:
Step-free street access is available directly to the Stalls via the dedicated accessible entrance on Station Street (intercom connected, met by an Access Host). 
Up to 8 dedicated wheelchair positions with step-free transfer seating are available along the Stalls aisles. 
A ground-floor RADAR-key accessible toilet is located on the Stalls level. 
General bathrooms are on the small side due to the age of the venue.
Please note the venue does not have a customer lift; the Dress Circle and Grand Upper Circle are accessible via stairs only. 
Sennheiser infrared and induction loop systems are available at the box office.
relaxed:
The Alexandra regularly schedules dedicated Relaxed, Audio Described, Captioned, and BSL-interpreted performances for touring musicals and family shows.
During relaxed performances, house lighting remains on low throughout the show, abrupt lighting transitions are moderated, and sudden loud sound spikes or pyrotechnics are softened.
An open-door policy permits families to come and go from the auditorium freely at any point. Dedicated quiet breakout spaces and foyer chill-out areas are available for sensory decompression, supported by trained Access Hosts. The upstairs lounge and bar area is a great space to decompress during the performance if necessary and the team are fantastic!
